title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: Consider estimating parameter \(\theta\) (e.g., \(L_{50}\)) sex:

title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: Assume sexes share identical parameters: \[\theta_{\text{female}} = \theta_{\text{male}} = \theta\] Problem: Ignores real biological differences sexes.

title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: Estimate sex independently: \[\theta_{\text{female}} \perp \theta_{\text{male}}\] Problem: Ignores sexes species. sparse sex gets unreliable estimates.

title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: Model sex-specific parameters draws common distribution: \[\theta_s \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \tau^2)\] \(\mu\) species-level mean \(\tau\) controls -sex variation. Key insight: model learns \(\tau\) data: sexes similar → small \(\tau\) → estimates shrink together sexes different → large \(\tau\) → estimates stay separated Sparse sex → borrows strength data-rich sex

title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: numerical stability, vitalBayes uses non-centered parameterization: \[\log(\theta_s) = \mu + \tau \cdot \eta_s, \quad \eta_s \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)\] separates global mean (\(\mu\)) sex-specific deviations (\(\eta_s\)), dramatically improves MCMC sampling \(\tau\) small.

title: Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
text: -sex standard deviation uses half-normal prior: \[\tau \sim \text{Half-Normal}(0, \sigma_\tau)\] \(\sigma_\tau\) set via prior_tau argument. prior: Allows \(\tau = 0\) (complete pooling) data support Permits large \(\tau\) sexes genuinely differ Avoids heavy tails half-Cauchy can cause divergences

text: Traditional growth models estimate \(k\) directly, \(k\) \(L_\infty\) strongly negatively correlated (often r < −0.9), making poorly identified data don’t extend near-asymptotic sizes. solution: Derive \(k\) observable maturity milestones: \[k = \frac{1}{t_{mat}} \ln\left(\frac{L_\infty - L_0}{L_\infty - L_{mat}}\right)\] parameterization: - Uses quantities fall within data range (\(L_{mat}\), \(t_{mat}\)) - Ensures biological consistency: growth curve passes maturity point - Propagates uncertainty upstream maturity models

what: 3. Partial Pooling for Imbalanced Sex Ratios
title: vitalBayes
text: problem: Elasmobranch sampling frequently yields imbalanced sex ratios. dataset might contain 150 females 34 males. Fitting separate models produces: Wide, unreliable credible intervals sparse sex Estimates driven influential observations Inefficient use information (sexes species) Complete pooling (ignoring sex) biologically unrealistic. pooling (fully separate) wastes information. solution: Partial pooling models sex-specific parameters draws common distribution: \[\log(\theta_s) = \mu + \tau \cdot \eta_s, \quad \eta_s \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)\] μ population mean, τ -sex standard deviation, ηs standardized sex deviations. model learns τ data: sexes appear similar → small τ → estimates shrink together sexes appear different → large τ → estimates stay separated Sparse sex → borrows strength data-rich sex Non-centered parameterization: use non-centered form (estimating η rather θ directly) dramatically improves MCMC sampling τ small. -sex variation minimal, centered parameterizations create “funnel” geometry causes divergent transitions. Half-normal prior τ: place τ ~ Half-Normal(0, στ) rather commonly-used half-Cauchy. half-Cauchy’s heavy tails can pull τ toward implausibly large values, especially two groups (sexes). half-normal provides gentle regularization still allowing substantial -sex variation warranted. See vignette("partial_pooling") comprehensive treatment.
code: # Enable partial pooling (especially useful for imbalanced data) data(imbalanced_data)  # 150 females, 34 males  fit <- fit_bayesian_maturity(   maturity    = "mat",   lt          = "fl",    sex         = "sex",   data        = imbalanced_data[embryo == FALSE],   use_pooling = TRUE,    # Hierarchical structure   prior_tau   = 0.5      # Half-normal scale (on log scale) )  # Sex-specific estimates with appropriate shrinkage fit$summary("L50")  # Between-sex difference (still estimable!) fit$summary("L50_diff")

title: vitalBayes
text: problem: Bayesian models require prior distributions, specifying priors log-transformed parameters unintuitive. σ = 0.5 log(\(L_{50}\)) mean practical terms? Researchers often resort “weakly informative” priors without considering whether encode reasonable biological information. solution: vitalBayes uses coefficient variation (CV) prior specification. CV expresses uncertainty proportion mean — scale-invariant, intuitive quantity. parameter θ prior mean μ CV = c: - prior SD original scale σθ = μ · c - Approximately 95% prior mass falls within μ ± 2μc Example: Setting CV_Linf = 0.2 species expected \(L_\infty\) ≈ 100 cm means: - Prior SD ≈ 20 cm - 95% prior interval ≈ 60–140 cm far interpretable specifying σ = 0.2 log(\(L_\infty\)).
code: growth_fit <- fit_bayesian_growth(   lt   = "fl",   age  = "age",   data = growth_data[embryo == FALSE],      # Intuitive CV-based priors   CV_Linf = 0.20,    # 20% uncertainty on asymptotic length   CV_L0   = 0.30,    # 30% uncertainty on birth length   CV_Lmat = 0.20,    # 20% uncertainty on length-at-maturity   CV_tmat = 0.30     # 30% uncertainty on age-at-maturity )

title: vitalBayes
text: problem: Life history parameters typically estimated independently, ignoring biological connections. Birth size estimated embryo data, maturity reproductive assessments, growth age-length pairs—analysis producing point estimates confidence intervals don’t propagate downstream analyses. solution: vitalBayes implements integrated workflow posterior distributions flow forward life history stages: pass birth_fit, L50_fit, t50_fit fit_bayesian_growth(), function extracts posterior summaries constructs informative priors. Uncertainty upstream models propagates naturally growth parameter estimates. matters: - Biological coherence: Growth curves constrained pass maturity milestones - Proper uncertainty: Imprecise maturity estimates → wider growth parameter CIs - Information efficiency: available data inform final estimates - Reproducibility: entire workflow encapsulated function calls

title: Fit Bayesian Individual Growth Models — fit_bayesian_growth
text: von Bertalanffy (model = "v"): $$L(t) = L_\infty - (L_\infty - L_0) e^{-kt}$$ Gompertz (model = "g"): $$L(t) = L_\infty \exp\left(-\ln\left(\frac{L_\infty}{L_0}\right) e^{-kt}\right)$$ Logistic (model = "l"): $$L(t) = \frac{L_\infty}{1 + \left(\frac{L_\infty}{L_0} - 1\right) e^{-kt}}$$

title: Fit Bayesian Individual Growth Models — fit_bayesian_growth
text: Priors constructed using coefficient variation (CV) arguments: Linf: Prior mean defaults 1.05 * Lmax, Lmax maximum observed length (including incomplete cases without age data). prior SD mean * CV_Linf. Users can override Lmax via Lmax argument. k: Prior mean estimated data solving growth equation k observation averaging. Prior SD mean * CV_k. L0, Lmat, tmat: Can informed prior birth/maturity model fits, specified manually.
